item.title: From energy crisis to energy transition: How renewables are reshaping energy security
item.description: The continuing conflict in the Middle East is disrupting global energy markets and pushing up fuel prices, with knock-on effects far beyond the region.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Rising seas are sinking futures’
item.description: World leaders approved the UN Declaration on Sea Level Rise by consensus on Thursday as the UN chief warned that encroaching waters are already threatening the future of coastal communities worldwide.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: LIVE: World leaders approve new declaration to tackle rising sea levels
item.description: Sea level rise is among the most visible consequences of global warming, but for some countries, it is an imminent existential threat. World leaders approved a new declaration on Thursday while debating the best ways to strengthen international cooperation and support vulnerable low-lying nations most at risk.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Guterres calls on countries to set clear timelines for transition away from fossil fuels
item.description: “We are the first generation with the tools to end the fossil fuel age – and the last who can avert climate catastrophe,” UN Secretary-General António Guterres said on Wednesday, calling on countries to draw up credible roadmaps with clear timelines to transition away from fossil fuels.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: LIVE: Climate change is here - What happens next is still in our hands
item.description: From deadly floods in the Himalayas to wildfires and extreme heat across Europe, 2026 has brought a succession of stark reminders of a changing climate. The task is immediate: Protect people from the impacts already unfolding while rapidly cutting the emissions of harmful gasses driving climate change. World leaders have been meeting on Wednesday to discuss how to turn those priorities into action.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: When a country goes underwater: Island States fight for their future
item.description: Rising sea levels and ever-more-powerful storms are eroding shorelines, submerging land and threatening to evict millions of people from their homes worldwide.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: How El Niño offers a test of whether the world can adapt to a changing climate
item.description: El Niño is strengthening in a world that is already hotter, raising the risk of drought, floods and crop losses across some of the world’s most important food-producing regions. But unlike many disasters, this one can be seen coming. UN experts say the months ahead offer countries a chance not only to protect the next harvest and our food security, but to prepare for a more unpredictable climate in the long run.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: In Tanzania, the sea is moving inland – and taking livelihoods with it
item.description: Along the coast of Tanzania, in East Africa, the Indian Ocean is pushing saltwater ever farther inland, shrinking coconut harvests, driving fish away and leaving some residents wondering how much longer they can stay.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Why climate action now comes down to speed, finance and cooperation
item.description: Temporarily exceeding the 1.5°C global warming goal set in Paris is widely considered inevitable. The challenge now is to keep that overshoot as small and short as possible by cutting emissions faster, unlocking finance and strengthening international cooperation.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Less than 4 years from development goals deadline, progress shows what’s possible
item.description: For Benin, making progress on the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) has meant finding new ways to finance development.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: As freshwater reserves shrink, countries must prepare for a new water reality
item.description: The world is entering a period in which abnormal water supplies are becoming the norm, with river flows, groundwater and glaciers all showing signs of sustained disruption, the UN weather agency warned on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Highly persistent toxic waste threatens ‘many, if not all, human rights’
item.description: Poor management of toxic chemicals and hazardous waste threatens “many, if not all, human rights,” the newly appointed independent human rights independent expert on the rising threat told the Human Rights Council on Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: The world just had the hottest August ever
item.description: Earth just had the hottest August on record, according to newly released weather data.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN climate chief warns political division is undermining fight against ‘economic security emergency’
item.description: The head of the UN's climate body has warned that treating global warming as a partisan issue is dangerously out of step with reality, as he set out a stark account of the economic toll climate change is already inflicting on Europe.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘The water comes up to our knees’: Climate hazards shut millions of children out of school in 2025
item.description: When the creek beside Taudibura Garo's school in Papua New Guinea floods, the water doesn't stop at the gate. It rises through the pit toilets – making the school unsafe – sending the 16-year-old and her classmates home without being able to finish.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Flood-ravaged Nepal calls for climate justice
item.description: Nepal’s call for financial compensation following recent deadly floods underlines the need to help countries that contribute the least to climate change – but are increasingly grappling with its most lethal consequences, the top UN official in the country said on Wednesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: AI datacentres pose growing threat to electricity systems worldwide
item.description: Use of data-intensive technologies – in particular artificial intelligence (AI) data centres – is growing faster than electricity infrastructure can handle, the UN’s economic commission for Europe has warned, raising concerns about the future reliability and resilience of energy systems worldwide.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Coordinated action on clean air and climate change can net $15 for every dollar spent
item.description: Tackling air pollution and climate change together can save millions of lives, reduce global warming and generate roughly $15 in economic benefits for every $1 spent, a new UN-backed report has revealed.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: As wildfires spread north, UN agencies race to help Europe adapt
item.description: As the climate warms, the threat of wildfires is spreading in Europe. How can historically cooler and wetter countries prepare?
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Central Park adapts to climate change while helping New York stay cool
item.description: In the heart of Manhattan in New York City, the effects of climate change are becoming increasingly visible.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: El Niño is surging. Months of extreme heat could follow
item.description: Fuelled by exceptionally warm Pacific waters, the El Niño climate pattern is intensifying and has yet to peak. Forecasters are almost certain it will persist through February 2027 – with unusually warm conditions expected across much of the world in the coming months.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Fight for humanity’: Avoiding a climate catastrophe means acting now
item.description: Record heat waves, deadly flooding and extreme weather reflect an ever-warming planet poised to soon breach safe temperature limits, according to a UN report released on Tuesday, but doubling down on climate action now could avoid a climate catastrophe.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘The lake is our life’: Protecting a shared lifeline in Uganda
item.description: On the shores of Nkondo, in Uganda’s Kikuube district, the day begins before sunrise. Fishers enter the lake to fish, while families around Lake Albert rely on its waters for food, income and daily survival.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Rising seas, rising stakes: What increasing sea levels mean to humanity
item.description: The ocean is rising faster now than at any point in recorded history. The impacts are already being felt and the threats are growing.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: As the Himalayas melt, deadly floods become the new normal
item.description: A day before a wall of ice, rock and muddy water tore through Himalayan valleys along the Nepal-China border, Dipesh Chapagain was discussing with a colleague just how devastating such a disaster could be.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Immense impact’ of Nepal flood disaster highlighted as casualties mount
item.description: The impact of the deadly flood in Nepal has been described as “immense” as the authorities there confirm that 538 bodies have been recovered from the disaster-stricken area.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Shock and devastation remain, a day after Himalayan flood disaster
item.description: Amid reports that hundreds of people are still missing in Nepal and China after a floodwater surge slammed into towns and villages on Wednesday, aid teams have been working to reach communities cut off by the disaster.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Land models sprout as degradation threatens billions of livelihoods
item.description: Promising efforts to restore degraded land are now in the spotlight at a time when 40 per cent of the world’s land currently faces degradation and drought, threatening the livelihoods of over three billion people, the head of the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) said Wednesday, announcing three winners of its World Restoration Flagships awards.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Land degradation is costing far more than restoring: UN deputy chief
item.description: Countries are spending too little to restore degraded land even as the economic cost of doing nothing climbs towards $1 trillion a year, UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed warned at a major UN land conference in Mongolia.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Japan’s ‘2050 Weather Forecast’ highlights extreme heat in the future
item.description: As extreme heat becomes an increasingly visible reality across Japan, meteorologists, scientists, businesses and professional footballers are joining forces to encourage stronger climate action and raise awareness of the risks posed by global warming.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
